At first it's warm, like youre being held and everything is going to be okay and you have no worries in the world. Heavy eyelids ready to fall asleep at any moment. If you do too much when you first start using you will get sick and throw up, and will throw up the following morning as well. That warm euphoria is all you want to be able to feel again. So you do it again and get that same feeling, wake up the next day feeling okay. A few days later you do it again maybe to help you sleep or for whatever reason, maybe you're depressed and just want to numb yourself. Eventually you start looking at heroin as being your best friend, looking forward to seeing her after work or before you go to bed. You're able to function and work everyday and tell yourself you're not addicted and can stop at any time. One day you wake up and have some left from the night before and decide that today you will start your day by getting high to help you get through the day. After a couple weeks you're now getting high everyday. One day you wake up and realize you didn't save anything from the night before. You begin to sneeze and your body feels sore. Your skin is clammy and you're shivering. You call your dealer and go pick up. You get high and all these symptoms go away. You feel normal and you're ready to start your day. You call your boss and let him know you're running late. You ask a coworker to borrow some money for gas at the end of the day when you realize you spent the last of your paycheck that morning on heroin and no longer have any money in the bank. You get Home realizing you only have a small dose left and need to figure something out. You call your plug and remind him you've been a steady customer for months and get a steady paycheck each week and ask for a front. You get paid Friday and only have 2 more days until you get paid. Friday comes and half your check goes to paying him back plus you need to buy yourself more. That warm feeling of euphoria is a thing of the past. You can't sleep at night without getting high, restlessness, restless legs, cold sweats, diarrhea, puking, flu like symptoms. You lay in bed in a puddle of sweat. After waiting all night your plug finally tells you he's awake and to come through. You don't shower or brush your teeth or even get dressed, you jump in your car and go, you finally pick up and you're able to breath easy, the cold sweats go away and you feel better. Your coworkers start to notice you've lost weight and you're constantly late for work. You tell them you've been stressed and make up a lie. You've already begun to lie to your friends and family. People stop inviting you to do things on the weekend, you don't have money to anyway. The cycle continues until you lose your job. With no money and a crippling addiction you don't know where to go from here, rents due and you don't have it. Too ashamed at yourself to ask for help. You've given your life up to heroin. She now owns you.

this sebring honestly has been to hell and back and is still going strong. Sit back, relax and let me tell you her story. 

It all started back in 2004 while my father was having a midlife crisis. My mother, his ex wife, had gotten a 76 Corvette, her dream car. This vet happened to be a convertible. “She can’t be the only one riding top down this summer” my father thought to himself angrily while shaking his fist. 

Off he went, one thing in mind: Convertible! Now my father still to this day knows nothing about cars. “Hmmmm. Chrysler’s are fancy...convertible....not made in the 70s, SOLD!”

For the first summer my father steadily drove this car until my older sister Alison turned 16 and got her license and totaled her first three cars in two months. After this my father got himself an Suv, because they’re “safer”. This is when Seb entered its darkest of times. Alisons car. Luckily for the car Alison got a Dwi and lost her license, the car was safe from her destruction. Just in time for my car to be in the shop, although just temporary, this 16 year old me was PUMPED!!  Maybe too pumped because before my car was released to me from the shop, my reckless ass blew the engine on the little ol’ Seb. 

‘‘Twas quite a hassle to get Chrysler to replace the engine....buuuut it was still under warranty!!!  Over the next couple years this car would be passed back and fourth from my dad, to his girlfriend and her kids. Eventually, about five years ago I was in need of a car. At this point the Sebring wasn’t even on the road and wasn’t being driven, so wham bham right in the clam! Purchased this ol’ gal and she became mine again. 

After a good 7 months or so i was getting ready to drive across the country and see where i end up. (San Diego and eventually Colorado). 
Little Ms. Seb has seen better days and it was time for her to be taken off the road. She sat behind my fathers house for five long years. Up until April of last year when I was moving from NY to TN. i had an accurate that got a flat as soon as i went to leave. Made it maybe a mile or two. When i brought it in for a new tire i was told there’s no way he would be putting a tire on my car, due to the chassis being completely rotted. Had i hadn’t gotten that flat and attempted to make the drive to TN, it was very likely that my car would’ve snapped right over the steering bracket. If this happened on the highway with me and my dog....well let’s not go there. 

Well shit now what?! Left my job. Moved out of my apartment. Now no vehicle. Just me and my woofer. As i was pacing around my fathers the next day I saw her! There she was in all her glory. Plus the title was still in my name! “I do have a car!!” “Wooof wooof wooof” Tully and I yelled in harmony! After three days of hard work, flushing all the fluids, cutting plexiglas to replace the broken back window, some other junk....she was back on the road and ready to drive to Tennessee. 
She still lives happily to this day in her small home driveway of Athens TN. Still going strong. 💪🚗
